pvpTeams.name: Mimikyu balance
pvpTeams.plan: Use the Disguise-like shield pressure up front, preserve Snorlax as the neutral Body Slam pivot, and save Empoleon for closing Steel/Water coverage.

pvpTeams.name: Altaria control
pvpTeams.plan: Altaria pressures Fighters and Grass, Jellicent absorbs neutral play, and Tinkaton closes into Dragons and Fairies when Ground is controlled.

pvpTeams.name: Virizion anti-core
pvpTeams.plan: Lead Virizion into the Steel/Water core, pivot to Snorlax as the neutral Body Slam wall, and close with the buffed Iron Head of Corviknight.

pvpTeams.name: Giratina balance
pvpTeams.plan: Giratina supplies bulk, Shadow Empoleon flips tempo with damage, and Florges is held for Dragon or Dark cleanup.

pvpTeams.name: Origin Palkia balance
pvpTeams.plan: Origin Palkia leads with fast neutral pressure, Crowned Zacian absorbs Dragon/Fairy alignment, and Ho-Oh closes when Rock threats are removed.

pvpTeams.name: Origin Dialga water-fairy
pvpTeams.plan: Origin Dialga anchors the lead, Kyogre draws out Water answers, and Xerneas closes into Dragons and Dark types.

pvpTeams.name: Quagsire water-flying trap
pvpTeams.plan: Lead Shadow Quagsire to bait Grass answers, pivot to Feraligatr for Steel/Fire, and close with the Flying/Water bulk of Mantine against the Grass and Fighting that Quagsire draws.

pvpTeams.name: Melmetal flexible bulk
pvpTeams.plan: Lead Melmetal for Double Iron Bash pressure, pivot to Galarian Corsola to absorb Fighting and Ghost, and close with Fairy/Water coverage from Azumarill.

pvpTeams.name: Jellicent anti-Steel balance
pvpTeams.plan: Lead Jellicent to wall Water and Ghost leads, pivot to Corviknight against Fairies and Steels, and close with Mud Bomb from Quagsire to break the Steel core.

pvpTeams.name: Kingdra fairy lure
pvpTeams.plan: Lead Kingdra to bait Fairy switches, pivot to Shadow Sableye to punish Ghosts and Psychics, and close with Weather Ball from Ninetales against the Steels and Bugs Kingdra draws.

pvpTeams.name: Mimikyu steel closer
pvpTeams.plan: Mimikyu leads with broad neutral pressure, Cresselia absorbs bad alignment and scouts Dark or Ghost coverage, and Registeel closes once Fighters, Fire, and Ground threats are softened.

pvpTeams.name: Zygarde electric punish
pvpTeams.plan: Complete Zygarde anchors the lead, Shadow Empoleon pivots for immediate pressure and draws Electric responses, and Talonflame closes after Rock and Water answers have been exposed.

pvpTeams.name: Virizion ice-water core
pvpTeams.plan: Virizion pressures Water, Ground, and Steel leads, Lapras is the bulky pivot that draws Electric or Fighting answers, and Corviknight closes after shared Fire and Electric threats are managed.

pvpTeams.name: Dusknoir neutral pivot
pvpTeams.plan: Lead Dusknoir as the neutral Ghost pivot, swap to Feraligatr for Hydro Cannon pressure on Steels, and close with the raw bulk of Dondozo.

pvpTeams.name: Lunala crowned balance
pvpTeams.plan: Lunala leads with heavy Ghost pressure, Origin Palkia is the flexible neutral pivot, and Crowned Zacian closes after Fire and Ground answers are revealed.

pvpTeams.name: White Kyurem dragon pressure
pvpTeams.plan: White Kyurem leads with Dragon and Ice pressure, Reshiram pivots to punish Steel responses, and Xerneas closes after opposing Steel types and Dragon shields are depleted.

pvpTeams.name: Marshadow steel-water balance
pvpTeams.plan: Marshadow opens with fast Ghost pressure and Close Combat threat, Metagross pivots into Fairy and Dragon alignment, and Kyogre closes once Grass and Electric counters are removed.

pvpTeams.name: Melmetal dragon closer
pvpTeams.plan: Melmetal leads with rapid Steel pressure, Yveltal pivots to draw Fairy and Ice answers, and Shadow Garchomp closes once those shared counters and opposing shields are gone.

pvpTheorycraft.note: Next-season PvP theorycraft. Hand-curated from the official season announcement (via Pokemon GO Hub's attack-changes writeup) BEFORE the season's computed rankings exist. Every projection here is explicitly a projection: the battle-source re-base shortly after the season starts replaces guesses with computed standings, and this file should be updated or retired then. Move from/to values are the announced trainer-battle values; the announcement did not publish exact energy numbers for every change.

projections.name: Lickilicky
projections.why: Already the GL #1 and its core Body Slam got BUFFED (55 to 65). The higher energy cost slows its bait game slightly, but nothing else in the top ten got stronger. Shadow Ball (its second move) trims 100 to 90 — a graze, not a wound.

projections.name: Corviknight
projections.why: BOTH its charged moves got changed upward: Iron Head 70 to 85 (free damage, same cost) and Air Cutter 45 to 60. Sitting #19 with two buffed moves and no meta predator buffed alongside it. Also a UL riser for the same reason.

projections.name: Skarmory
projections.why: Classic GL royalty that fell off because Steel and Rock walled its Flying damage. Drill Run (Ground) hits exactly those walls. Sky Attack pressure plus Ground coverage is the old Skarmory nightmare, re-armed.

projections.name: Greninja
projections.why: Water Shuriken is one of the fastest energy fast moves in the game and it finally gets a cheap spam move worth that energy: Brutal Swing (Dark). Ghost/Psychic teams have a new problem. Its glass Attack stat is the tradeoff — it deletes things or gets deleted.

projections.name: Raichu
projections.why: Volt Tackle (also on Alolan Raichu) gives it a real Electric nuke. Probably a cup star more than an open-GL core, but the re-base will say.

projections.name: Tinkaton
projections.why: Untouched by the rebalance — but the Twitch drop handed one to every player, so expect it on far more ladders. Fairy/Steel still beats Dragons, Darks, and Fairies wholesale.

projections.name: Jellicent
projections.why: Its core Shadow Ball ate the 100-to-90 nerf with no compensation. Still bulky, still Water/Ghost, but the kill threshold moves against it.

projections.name: Umbreon
projections.why: Shadow Ball nerf trims its closer. The bulk and Foul Play pressure are untouched — it stays a safe-swap staple, just slightly less lethal on the long game.

projections.name: Grimmsnarl
projections.why: New Draining Kiss at 80 power with a GUARANTEED Defense raise every throw — a Dark/Fairy that gets tankier as the fight runs. Unproven, but the effect compounds.

projections.name: Gallade
projections.why: Sacred Sword is cheap Fighting damage on a mon that also carries Psycho Cut energy and Shadow/Psychic coverage — the anti-Steel, anti-Dark toolkit UL rewards. Needs a male Ralts/Kirlia line and a Sinnoh Stone.

projections.name: Lickilicky
projections.why: Same Body Slam buff carries to the XL build. Expensive (Level 48+, XL candy), but the payoff rises with the move.

projections.name: Annihilape
projections.why: Rage Fist 50 to 55 but at higher cost. Hits harder, cycles slower; whether that nets positive depends on breakpoints the re-base will surface.

projections.name: Lugia
projections.why: Lugia's eternal problem is the Steel core — Dialga, Metagross, Melmetal — walling Aeroblast. Earth Power hits every one of them super-effectively. The wall-breaker it has waited years for.

projections.name: Dialga
projections.why: Iron Head 70 to 85 is a direct buff to Dialga's own charged move. The ML anchor got handed more damage for nothing — though new Earth Power Lugia is a fresh predator.

projections.name: Darkrai
projections.why: Two new Dark moves at once. Sucker Punch gives it a real fast move, Foul Play a mid-cost charge. Glass, but ML Ghost/Psychic staples (Mewtwo, Lunala, Giratina) all hate it.
